items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you recall seeing — I think it’s the Glenn Miller movie, and Ben Pollack is in it? [INTERVIEWEE] Sure is, and the Benny Goodman Story too.

ctx.x: They sure did, yeah. The older players tended to use larger bass drums, and maybe two tom-toms. Floor tom, two mounted toms, wood block, two cowbells, and the cymbals down low, snare drum toted way over, which is a hold over from marching bands, when it’s slung over your shoulder you play like you would in a military band. But all the Chicago drummers learned rudiments and classical technique from drummers who had come out of that military and classical tradition. So they played like that and lifted their sticks…
Do you recall seeing — I think it’s the Glenn Miller movie, and Ben Pollack is in it?
Sure is, and the Benny Goodman Story too.
